issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Recipe steps: the FIRST cooking instruction is rendered as an unnumbered bullet '•' labeled (for screen readers) 'Recipe note:' — as if it were a preamble — and every remaining step is numbered off-by-one with the step count one short. A 6-step recipe shows an unnumbered first step, then 'Step 1 of 5' … 'Step 5 of 5'.

Route: /recipe-detail (open any recipe meal from Nutrition → the 'Instructions' section). Also affects the collapsible 'Recipe' block on the meal-detail screen.

Expected: instructions render 'Step 1 of N' … 'Step N of N', the first real step numbered 1. Actual: the first instruction shows a '•' bullet + aria-label 'Recipe note: <first step>', numbering starts at '1' on the SECOND step, and the total is N-1.

Root cause (src/components/RecipeStepList.tsx): the renderer UNCONDITIONALLY treats finalSteps[0] as a preamble — isPreamble = (i === 0) (lines 100 & 132), stepNum = i (so the 2nd element becomes 'Step 1'), and totalSteps = finalSteps.length - 1 (line 90). That is only correct when a leading preamble was actually extracted. But (a) the `steps` prop — used by RecipeDetail as steps={recipe.instructions} — is documented at line 48 as 'Pre-split step strings' with NO preamble, so instructions[0] is a real step; and (b) splitRecipeSteps(notes) only prepends a preamble element when preamble TEXT precedes the first marker — for the common notes that start directly with '1) …' it returns pure steps (see the component's own test, lines 170-174), so notes[0] is also a real step.

Node-verified render decision (replicating lines 90/100/101/108/116):
CASE A steps=['Heat oil…','Add onions…','Add spices…','Serve hot'] -> '[•] Recipe note: Heat oil…' / 'Step 1 of 3: Add onions…' / 'Step 2 of 3' / 'Step 3 of 3' (4 instructions shown as 1 note + 3 numbered).
CASE B notes='1) Boil pasta 2) Make sauce 3) Combine' -> splits to 3 real steps -> first shown as '[•] Recipe note: Boil pasta', then 'Step 1 of 2' / 'Step 2 of 2'.
CASE C notes WITH a genuine preamble ('Prep + cook ~20 min. 1) …') renders correctly — confirming the code only works when a preamble is actually present.

Repro: 1) Open /recipe-detail for any recipe whose instructions start with the first step (i.e. no 'Prep ~X min' preamble). 2) Scroll to Instructions. Expected step 1 is shown as an unnumbered bullet and the visible numbering / 'Step k of M' count is off by one.

Fix: only treat index 0 as a preamble when it genuinely is one (e.g. have splitRecipeSteps return a hasPreamble flag or prepend a sentinel, or detect that element 0 lacks a leading numeric marker). For the `steps` prop path, number from 1 with totalSteps = length. The existing RecipeStepList tests do NOT lock the buggy path — they only seed a preamble at [0] and never assert numbering for the no-preamble / raw-`steps` cases.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements: typing a value into the measurement number field does nothing — the field silently reverts to the previously-logged value (or 0.00 if none) on the very next render, so a typed value can never be committed. Only the +/- stepper buttons work.

Repro: 1) Open /measurements. 2) Tap the large number field under "Record New Measurement". 3) Type any number (e.g. 45). Expected: field shows 45. Actual: field immediately snaps back to the seeded value (last-logged value for that body part, or 0.00 for a first-ever measurement).

Verified via Playwright on localhost:8080 with a mocked /measurements/ overview (seeded history=33 for Right Arm): typing "45" left the input at "33"; the + button by contrast updates correctly (33 -> steps).

Root cause: the re-seed effect in src/pages/Measurements.tsx (lines 310-321) re-runs on every render (its dep allTypeHistories is a fresh array each render from useQueries) and calls seedFromLatest() whenever userEdited.current is false, overwriting the input. The +/- buttons set userEdited.current=true (lines 580 & 589) so they are exempt, but the text <input> onChange (lines 560-567) never sets userEdited.current, so every keystroke is wiped. Same class as the prior QA i-20260704-22f4 fix (which guarded the steppers) — the text-input path was missed.

Fix: set userEdited.current=true inside the input onChange when a valid value is entered (mirror the stepper buttons). Impact: a first-ever measurement (0 seed) can otherwise only be reached by tapping + up to ~190 times to hit 95cm.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Typing a value into the Body Measurements field did nothing — it snapped back to the last-logged value (or 0) on the next render, because only the +/- buttons were treated as a user edit. The text field now records typed input as an edit too, so a typed value sticks. Proof: seeded to 33, typed 45, and it stayed 45.

judge.note: Root-cause fix mirrors the stepper's userEdited guard; regression test fails-before/passes-after; live screenshot shows typed 45 persisting over the 33 seed.

issues.description: [suggestion] One-tap "Repeat meal" on the Nutrition diary — long-press or a small repeat-icon on any past meal card re-logs the same food(s)/quantities to today with one confirm tap, instead of requiring the CustomMealModal. Problem: athletes eat the same breakfast/post-workout shake most days but must reopen the manual-entry modal, hunt the food again via search or the buried "Recent meals" chip row (CustomMealModal.tsx:514-533), and resubmit every time — friction that discourages consistent logging (the exact behavior daily-completion/streak scoring depends on). Evidence: repo scan confirmed barcode scan, water tracker, and streak-freeze already exist, but no true repeat-log exists anywhere in src/pages/Nutrition.tsx or src/pages/_components/nutrition/ — the closest is the modal's prefill-only "Recent meals" row, which still requires opening the modal and resubmitting. Comparable trackers (MyFitnessPal "Copy meal", Cronometer "Copy from previous day") ship this as a core retention feature. v1 scope: add a repeat icon/swipe action on each meal-diary row (today or yesterday) that calls the existing add-meal/log endpoint with the same food_items + quantities, no new backend route needed; skip cross-day "copy whole day" for v1. Effort: ~0.5-1 day FE-only (new button + reuse existing log-meal service call).
